For with Hashem, may He be blessed, it makes no difference
even if one prays in a whisper,
that comes from the depths of the heart,
so that one cannot articulate with his lips
but only cries out in a simple voice
from the pain of his heart.
And such a prayer is the most accepted,
"A prayer of the poor man when he is faint
and pours out his speech before Hashem":
for the prayer of the poor man
because "he pours out his speech before Hashem" —
that is, like one who pours out
his pain and worry before his friend
in order to ease the pain from his heart.
And this kind of language is found
regarding the Men of the Great Assembly,
"And they cried out in a loud voice," etc.;
that is, an outcry in a simple voice
from the depth of the heart's pain
over the greatness of the distress
of the provocation of the evil inclination.
And this is the meaning of
to the voice of my supplications":
for prayer requires a time of favor,
and it is not answered at all times.
